maize.general:
- Plant at onset of reliable rains
- Use certified seed
- Scout early for Fall Armyworm
- Critical moisture at tasseling & grain filling

Land Preparation.tips:
- Plough or rip to break hardpans
- Create a fine seedbed
- Ridge on sloping land
- Incorporate manure in drought-prone areas

Planting & Spacing.tips:
- Plant 3–7 cm deep
- Standard hybrids: 75 × 30 cm
- High-density hybrids: 75 × 25 cm
- OPVs: 90 × 30–35 cm

Fertilizer.tips:
- Apply basal DAP/TSP: 50–100 kg/ha
- Top-dress with CAN/Urea twice:
  • At 4–6 weeks
  • At knee-high stage
- Total N: 100–200 kg/ha for hybrids

Water & Irrigation.tips:
- Most critical stages:
  • Seedling establishment
  • Tasseling & silking
  • Grain filling
- Even drought-tolerant varieties need moisture at flowering

Pest & Disease.tips:
- Use FAW-tolerant varieties (reduces damage)
- Scout fields weekly
- Apply recommended insecticides early if needed
- For MLN: use certified seed + crop rotation

Harvest & Storage.tips:
- Harvest when grain moisture is ~20%
- Dry grains to ≤13% moisture content
- Store in hermetic bags (e.g. PICS, SuperGrain bags)
- Keep storage area clean and dry

KDH414 / Ukamez-1 (Drought-tolerant).tips:
- Excellent moisture conservation
- Use mulching and minimum tillage
- Apply moderate fertilizer rates
- Split nitrogen applications

FAWTH2001–2003 (FAW-tolerant).tips:
- Built-in tolerance reduces damage
- Still scout weekly
- Combine with pheromone traps & biopesticides
- Strong foundation for IPM

Katumani composites / OPVs.tips:
- Wider spacing: 90 × 30–35 cm
- Lower fertilizer requirement
- Excellent for marginal lands
- Farmers can recycle seed

ADC 6-series / High-altitude hybrids.tips:
- High yield potential
- Respond well to fertilizer (high input)
- Spacing: 75 × 25 cm
- Good tolerance to rust and GLS

beans.general:
- Inoculate seed with rhizobium (especially on new fields)
- Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer
- Critical moisture needed at flowering & pod filling

Land Preparation.tips:
- Achieve fine tilth
- Incorporate well-decomposed compost or manure
- Avoid wet or cloddy seedbeds

Planting & Spacing.tips:
- Plant 3–4 cm deep
- Bush beans: 45–60 × 10–15 cm
- Climbing beans: 75 × 30 cm + staking

Fertilizer.tips:
- Phosphorus is usually most limiting
- Apply TSP or DAP at planting
- Minimal nitrogen needed (especially if inoculated)
- Rhizobium inoculation highly recommended

Water & Irrigation.tips:
- Very sensitive to drought during flowering & pod filling
- Nyota variety has better drought tolerance
- Ensure consistent moisture during critical stages

Pest & Disease.tips:
- Watch for bean fly, aphids, and anthracnose
- Use certified clean seed
- Practice crop rotation
- Remove and burn affected plants

Harvest.tips:
- Harvest when pods are dry and seeds rattle
- Dry in shade to maintain seed color
- Thresh carefully to avoid splitting

Nyota (KAD-02).tips:
- Matures in 60–70 days
- High iron and zinc content
- Good drought tolerance
- Fast harvest = early income

Angaza (KMR-11).tips:
- Biofortified with iron and zinc
- Mid-maturity: 75–80 days
- Good yield under moderate management

Metameta (KMR-12).tips:
- Uniform maturity
- Easy synchronized harvesting
- Good for group marketing

irish_potatoes.general:
- Always use certified seed tubers
- Ideal soil pH: 5.5–6.5
- Hill soil regularly to prevent greening
- Stop irrigation when foliage starts yellowing

Land Preparation.tips:
- Plough to 20–30 cm depth
- Remove nightshade weeds
- Form ridges 25–40 cm high

Planting & Spacing.tips:
- Use certified seed tubers only
- Cut large tubers and heal for 2–3 days
- Shangi & standard: 75 × 30 cm
- Processing varieties: 75–90 × 35 cm
- Plant 10–15 cm deep

Fertilizer.tips:
- Apply well-decomposed manure: 5–10 t/ha OR
- NPK 17:17:17 at 250 kg/ha at planting
- Top-dress CAN at 35–45 days
- Increase potassium for processing varieties

Water & Irrigation.tips:
- Total water need: 450–600 mm
- Critical stages:
  • Tuber initiation
  • Bulking phase
- Avoid waterlogging

Pest & Disease.tips:
- Late blight: apply protectant fungicides regularly
- Bacterial wilt: 3–5 year rotation + certified seed
- Use resistant varieties where possible

Harvest & Storage.tips:
- Shangi: harvest at 70–90 days
- Processing varieties: 100–130 days
- Cure tubers in shade for 7–14 days
- Store in cool, dark, well-ventilated area

Shangi.tips:
- Very early maturity: 70–90 days
- High market demand
- Degenerates fast → always use certified seed
- Short dormancy → sell quickly

Kenya Mpya / Tigoni.tips:
- Improved late blight tolerance
- Reliable yield in cool areas
- Standard spacing and management

Markies / Asante.tips:
- High dry matter content
- Long season (100–130 days)
- Excellent storage life
- Responds well to high potassium

Unica.tips:
- Heat and drought tolerant
- Good performance with organic matter
- Strong disease resistance

tomatoes.general:
- Stake and prune indeterminate varieties
- Avoid wetting leaves during irrigation
- Apply calcium foliar sprays to prevent blossom-end rot

Land Preparation.tips:
- Use raised beds in heavy soils
- Incorporate well-rotted manure
- Ensure good drainage

Nursery & Transplanting.tips:
- Raise seedlings for 4–6 weeks
- Transplant at 4–6 true leaves stage
- Determinate: 60 × 45 cm
- Indeterminate: 90 × 60 cm

Fertilizer.tips:
- Apply basal NPK at planting
- Increase potassium during fruiting stage
- Regular calcium foliar sprays
- Monitor for micronutrient deficiencies

Water & Irrigation.tips:
- Provide even, frequent irrigation
- Drip irrigation is ideal
- Avoid water stress during flowering and fruit set

Pest & Disease.tips:
- Major threats: Tuta absoluta, whitefly, TYLCV, bacterial wilt
- Use resistant hybrids where possible
- Practice integrated pest management (IPM)
- Remove and destroy infected plants

Harvest.tips:
- Harvest at breaker stage for long-distance transport
- Firm hybrids have better shelf life
- Handle carefully to avoid bruising

Onyx F1.tips:
- Firm oval fruits
- Maturity: ~70 days
- Excellent shelf life and transport tolerance

Rio Grande.tips:
- Determinate growth habit
- Heat tolerant
- Uniform ripening

Tylka F1 / Buena Vista F1.tips:
- Strong resistance to TYLCV and bacterial wilt
- Vigorous plant growth
- High yield potential

carrots.general:
- Requires deep, stone-free soil (>30 cm)
- Needs continuous moisture
- Thin seedlings early
- Never use fresh manure

Land Preparation.tips:
- Dig deeply (>30 cm)
- Remove all stones and debris
- Create fine, level seedbed
- Use only well-rotted compost

Planting & Spacing.tips:
- Direct sow 1–2 cm deep
- Thin to 5–10 cm between plants
- Rows 25–30 cm apart

Fertilizer.tips:
- Apply moderate NPK at planting
- Avoid excess nitrogen (causes forking)
- Boron is critical to prevent hollow heart

Water & Irrigation.tips:
- Maintain even soil moisture throughout growth
- Avoid fluctuations (prevents cracking & forking)
- Light, frequent irrigation works best

Pest & Disease.tips:
- Carrot fly: use row covers or companion planting
- Nematodes: rotate with non-host crops
- Maintain healthy, loose soil

Harvest.tips:
- Harvest 70–110 days depending on variety
- Lift carefully to avoid breakage
- Cool immediately after harvest

Nantes.tips:
- Sweet flavor
- Cylindrical shape
- Good shelf life
- Maturity: 80–100 days

Kuroda / Super Kuroda.tips:
- Heat tolerant
- Thicker roots
- Good uniformity

Chantenay.tips:
- Shorter, stumpier roots
- Early maturity
- Good for home gardens

Nebula F1 / Sunrise F1.tips:
- Hybrid vigor
- Excellent disease tolerance
- High marketable yield

cabbage.general:
- Transplant when seedlings have 4–6 true leaves
- Maintain consistent moisture
- Apply boron to ensure good head formation

Land Preparation.tips:
- Deep plough the field
- Incorporate 8–10 t/ha well-decomposed manure
- Form raised beds if drainage is poor

Nursery & Transplanting.tips:
- Raise seedlings for 4–6 weeks
- Harden off before transplanting
- Spacing for hybrids: 60 × 45 cm

Fertilizer.tips:
- Apply basal manure + NPK at planting
- Top-dress nitrogen at 3 weeks and 6 weeks
- Ensure boron availability

Water & Irrigation.tips:
- Keep soil consistently moist for crisp heads
- Drip irrigation reduces fungal diseases
- Avoid water stress during head formation

Pest & Disease.tips:
- Diamondback moth, aphids, black rot common
- Use Bt sprays, neem, or approved insecticides
- Practice crop rotation and field hygiene

Harvest.tips:
- Harvest when heads are firm and compact
- Cut with a sharp knife
- Cool immediately after harvest

Gloria F1 / Queen F1.best_for: Large uniform heads for premium markets
Gloria F1 / Queen F1.tips:
- High yielding
- Excellent head weight
- Invest in good nursery and fertilizer

Pruktor F1.tips:
- Strong resistance to fusarium wilt
- Reliable performance in warm areas

Copenhagen Market (OPV).tips:
- Reliable open-pollinated variety
- Good head size
- Lower seed cost

kales.general:
- Allows multiple harvests (ratooning)
- Plant densely for higher yields
- Pick outer leaves regularly to encourage new growth

Land Preparation.tips:
- Incorporate plenty of manure
- Achieve fine tilth for good germination

Planting & Spacing.tips:
- Can direct sow or transplant
- Spacing: 30–45 × 30 cm
- Closer spacing = more tender leaves

Fertilizer.tips:
- Heavy feeder – loves nitrogen
- Apply basal manure + top-dress CAN twice
- Responds well to split applications

Water & Irrigation.tips:
- Moderately drought tolerant
- Yields drop significantly without water
- Regular irrigation = continuous harvest

Pest & Disease.tips:
- Aphids and diamondback moth common
- Use neem oil, wood ash, or Bt sprays
- Remove old leaves to reduce hiding spots

Harvest.tips:
- Start picking 4–6 weeks after transplanting
- Harvest outer leaves regularly
- Maintain fertility for continuous production

Collards / Thousand Headed.tips:
- Very cheap seed
- Extremely productive
- Long harvesting period

Mfalme F1 / Marrow Stem.tips:
- Higher market price
- Darker, more attractive leaves
- Higher yield than traditional types

onions.general:
- Transplant when seedlings are pencil-thick
- Reduce watering 2–3 weeks before harvest
- Cure bulbs properly for long storage

Land Preparation.tips:
- Deep cultivation for bulb development
- Create fine, level seedbed
- Form raised beds for drainage
- Incorporate 8–15 t/ha manure

Nursery & Transplanting.tips:
- Raise seedlings for 6–8 weeks
- Transplant at pencil thickness
- Spacing: 30 × 8–10 cm

Fertilizer.tips:
- Apply basal NPK at planting
- Top-dress with CAN + Sulphate of Potash (SOP)
- Sulphur improves pungency and storage

Water & Irrigation.tips:
- Provide light, frequent irrigation
- Stop watering 2–3 weeks before harvest
- Allows proper bulb curing in field

Pest & Disease.tips:
- Thrips: use blue sticky traps + neem
- Downy mildew: ensure good airflow
- Practice crop rotation

Harvest & Storage.tips:
- Harvest when 50–70% tops fall over
- Cure bulbs in shade for 7–14 days
- Store long-keeping varieties in well-ventilated area
- Trim tops after full curing

Bombay Red.tips:
- Heat tolerant
- Excellent keeper
- Good for long storage

Red Creole / Tropicana.tips:
- Pungent flavor
- Very good keeper
- Performs well in dry zones

Jambar F1 / Neptune F1.tips:
- Hybrid vigor
- Early maturity
- Large, uniform bulbs
- High marketable yield

Texas Grano 502.tips:
- Large, mild-flavored bulbs
- Short-day variety
- Great for salads and fresh use
